candidates.attacker_control: The HTTP `Content-Type` header of a request routed to Struts (unauthenticated, no special configuration required). Because `Dispatcher.wrapRequest` only requires the header to *contain* the substring "multipart/form-data" (not to be a valid multipart type), a header such as `%{(<OGNL expression containing the literal string 'multipart/form-data'>)}` both triggers the multipart wrapper and makes commons-fileupload raise an exception whose message embeds the full header. The request body/parameters are irrelevant.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: (1) Verified the bundle does contain a safe static message for SizeLimitExceededException/IOException (struts-messages.properties:35-36), so the size-limit path does not evaluate attacker text; only exception classes without a key fall back to `e.getMessage()`. (2) Verified `Dispatcher.wrapRequest` uses `content_type.contains("multipart/form-data")` (substring, not prefix/parse), so a payload containing that literal string still reaches the multipart parser even though commons-fileupload rejects it as non-multipart. (3) Checked that `cleanupActionName`/`checkSimpleMethod` hardening in `OgnlUtil` only constrains `OgnlUtil.callMethod` (action-method invocation), not `ValueStack.findValue`, which is the sink used by `translateVariables`. (4) Searched the repository for `InvalidContentTypeException` — no message-bundle entry exists anywhere, so the fallback path is reachable. (5) Confirmed `struts.multipart.parser=jakarta` in default.properties, so `JakartaMultiPartRequest` is the default implementation.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary OGNL expression evaluation in the server's request context (pre-authentication). Depending on the effective OGNL member-access restrictions of the deployed configuration, this ranges from sensitive data disclosure / denial of service up to remote code execution (the S2-045/CVE-2017-5638 exploitation pattern), and it occurs during error handling of an ordinary multipart-looking request. The same unsafe fallback pattern exists in `JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest` and `MultiPartRequestWrapper`.
candidates.prerequisites: Default Struts configuration (`struts.multipart.parser=jakarta` per core/src/main/resources/org/apache/struts2/default.properties:69; no `struts.messages.upload.error.InvalidContentTypeException` bundle key in any locale — verified absent repo-wide), request processed by the Struts filter so the multipart wrapper is created, and an ActionContext/value stack available when parsing runs (LocalizedTextUtil acquires it from ActionContext; the same code path is the published S2-045 vector). The commons-fileupload dependency is pinned at 1.3.1 (pom.xml:712-715), whose invalid-content-type error text embeds the supplied content type.
candidates.root_cause: `JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage` passes the exception's message (`e.getMessage()`, which for commons-fileupload parsing failures contains the raw attacker-supplied Content-Type header) as the `defaultMessage` to `LocalizedTextUtil.findText`. When the corresponding `struts.messages.upload.error.<Exception>` key is missing from all bundles (only SizeLimitExceededException and IOException keys exist), `LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage` treats that attacker text as a localizable pattern and calls `TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack)`, which parses `${...}`/`%{...}` and evaluates the inner text with `ValueStack.findValue(...)` (OGNL) under the current request's ActionContext/value stack. No validation or escaping of the fallback message is performed.
candidates.title: Untrusted multipart exception message (Content-Type) is evaluated as an OGNL expression during i18n fallback (S2-045/CVE-2017-5638 class)
candidates.trace: 1) Attacker sends POST with Content-Type containing "multipart/form-data" inside a `%{...}`/`${...}` payload. 2) `Dispatcher.wrapRequest` (Dispatcher.java:791-795) sees the substring and constructs `MultiPartRequestWrapper`, which calls `multi.parse(request, saveDir)` (MultiPartRequestWrapper.java:85-88). 3) `JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse` (lines 82-107) calls `processUpload` -> `parseRequest` -> commons-fileupload `ServletFileUpload.parseRequest`, which throws `InvalidContentTypeException` (or another FileUploadException) whose message includes the raw Content-Type. 4) The catch block calls `buildErrorMessage(e, ...)` (line 118), which resolves key `struts.messages.upload.error.<SimpleName>` via `LocalizedTextUtil.findText(this.getClass(), errorKey, defaultLocale, e.getMessage(), args)`. 5) No bundle provides that key (struts-messages.properties:34-36 only defines SizeLimitExceededException and IOException), so `findText` falls through to `getDefaultMessage` (LocalizedTextUtil.java:570-580, 714-737), where `message = defaultMessage` (the attacker text) and line 729 executes `TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack)`. 6) `TextParseUtil.translateVariables` (lines 46-48) delegates to the parser at lines 154-169, whose `ognlEval` calls `stack.findValue(parsedValue, asType)` — the `%{...}`/`${...}` content is evaluated as OGNL in the request's value-stack context, before the result is passed to `MessageFormat`.
candidates.unverified: The exact commons-fileupload 1.3.1 exception text could not be read (third-party binary; inferred from the pinned version and the documented `InvalidContentTypeException` message format). The presence of an ActionContext/value stack at the moment `MultiPartRequestWrapper` is constructed was not runtime-verified. Whether the OGNL member-access restrictions configured in this snapshot (struts-default.xml excludedClasses/excludedPackageNames, struts.ognl.allowStaticMethodAccess=false) fully permit the classic S2-045 RCE payload was not tested; expression evaluation itself is unconditional on this path. No runtime or exploit verification was performed.
candidates.weakness_type: Expression-language injection (OGNL) / arbitrary code execution (CWE-917, CWE-94)

coverage_summary: Source scope: 3,617 model-visible files (1 excluded by sensitive-name/path filter; binaries skipped). Relation index is partial: 1,948 Java files parsed, 520 files omitted, 24 parse errors, and it provides only syntactic candidates (no control/data flow, no semantic resolution). I inspected in depth: the multipart request path (Dispatcher.wrapRequest, MultiPartRequestWrapper, JakartaMultiPartRequest, JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest), i18n text lookup and evaluation (LocalizedTextUtil, TextParseUtil, XWorkConverter/DefaultActionProxy usage), OGNL plumbing (OgnlUtil, SecurityMemberAccess, OgnlValueStack), action mapping/DMI (DefaultActionMapper, RestActionMapper, Restful2ActionMapper, CompositeActionMapper, DefaultActionProxy, DefaultActionInvocation, StrutsActionProxyFactory), Parameter/Cookie/Debugging/I18n interceptors, static content loading, and the REST plugin's content handlers plus relevant unit tests and message bundles. Searched repo-wide for security-relevant markers (CVE-*, S2-0*, exploit/PWN payloads, vulnerability comments) and for message keys. Not deeply reviewed: most non-core plugins (json/jasperreports/embeddedjsp/dwr/oval/cdi/spring/portlet/tiles/velocity/freemarker), the apps/showcase and archetype sample code, assembly/docs, and the 24 unparsed Java files.
limitations: No runtime, test, or exploit execution; findings are source-evidence only and not runtime-confirmed.
Third-party dependency internals (commons-fileupload 1.3.1, OGNL 3.1.8, XStream) could not be read; their message/allow-list behavior is inferred from the pinned versions.
The P1 relation index is partial (520 omitted files, 24 parse errors, no data-flow/semantic resolution), so absence of an indexed relation is not evidence of absence.

The benchmark case identity could not be confirmed: the snapshot is a 2.5.1-SNAPSHOT development tree (mid-2016 dependency set), so several later-fixed Struts issues (S2-045/046, S2-052, S2-057, S2-059/061 classes) are all naturally present, and I could not determine from source alone which single fix commit the case corresponds to; the submitted candidate is the strongest source-backed issue, not a verified match.
Large parts of the tree (plugins, apps, archetypes, docs) were only surveyed, not line-by-line audited.

rejected_leads.lead: RestActionMapper path-based method extraction is not gated by struts.enable.DynamicMethodInvocation and does not pass through cleanupActionName (plugins/rest/.../RestActionMapper.java:221-234), while the same class gates the '!' form (lines 307-328).
rejected_leads.reason: Real inconsistency, but the REST plugin is designed to derive methods from URLs (/action/id/edit), existing tests (RestActionMapperTest.testEditMapping, testDeleteMapping, ...) assert exactly this behavior with DMI unset, and the method string reaching OgnlUtil.callMethod is constrained by the S2-032-era checkSimpleMethod guard (OgnlUtil.java:390-402), so I could not substantiate RCE or a clear contract violation from source alone. Kept as an unconfirmed lead.

rejected_leads.lead: XStreamHandler.toObject uses an unfiltered `new XStream()` for request bodies (plugins/rest/.../handler/XStreamHandler.java:43-50).
rejected_leads.reason: Definitely unsafe-looking and matching the later S2-052/XStream deserialization issue, but exploitability depends entirely on the XStream version/allow-listing behavior of the external library, which cannot be inspected here; no in-repo validation is missing beyond library-version choice, so it is a weaker, dependency-driven lead.

rejected_leads.lead: DefaultStaticContentLoader path handling with URLDecoder.decode and endsWith check (core/.../DefaultStaticContentLoader.java:182-208, 279-288).
rejected_leads.reason: The traversal guard (resourceUrl.getFile().endsWith(buildPath(...))) is present; no clear bypass was demonstrated during review, so it remains a hardening observation rather than a candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: DebuggingInterceptor 'command' mode evaluates a request-supplied `expression` via stack.findValue (core/.../debugging/DebuggingInterceptor.java:188-207).
rejected_leads.reason: Explicitly gated on struts.devMode (line 146-148), which defaults to false; not exploitable in a default deployment.

rejected_leads.lead: ParametersInterceptor and CookieInterceptor parameter/cookie injection into the value stack.
rejected_leads.reason: Both have the expected guards in this snapshot (accepted/excluded pattern checkers; ParameterNameAware; CookieInterceptor.isAcceptableName with a whitelist pattern), so no missing validation was established.
They inherit the hardened DefaultActionMapper behavior (DMI gate, cleanupActionName); no additional unguarded path was found.

summary:
Apache Struts 2.5.1-SNAPSHOT (core, plugins, apps, archetypes). The strongest source-evidenced issue is an expression-injection chain in the default multipart (Jakarta) error path: attacker-controlled text taken from the request's exception message (raw Content-Type header) is used as a localization "default message" that Struts then evaluates through `TextParseUtil.translateVariables` -> `ValueStack.findValue` (OGNL) with the request's value stack. This is the CVE-2017-5638 / S2-045 vulnerability class present in this snapshot. All links were verified in source: `Dispatcher.wrapRequest` selects the multipart wrapper on a mere substring match for "multipart/form-data" (Dispatcher.java:791-795), `JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse/buildErrorMessage` forwards `e.getMessage()` as the default message (JakartaMultiPartRequest.java:82-119), the upload-error keys in the message bundle only cover SizeLimitExceededException/IOException (struts-messages.properties:34-36), and `LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage` evaluates the fallback text with OGNL (LocalizedTextUtil.java:714-737, via TextParseUtil.java:46-48 and 154-169). The same pattern is duplicated in `JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest` and `MultiPartRequestWrapper`. Other plausible but weaker/rejected leads are listed below.

Note on case identity: the snapshot is a genuine mid-2016 2.5.1 dev tree (OGNL 3.1.8, commons-fileupload 1.3.1, log4j2 2.5, no HttpParameters), i.e. a version inside the affected ranges of several Struts advisories, not the parent of the S2-045 fix; I could not confirm from source alone which advisory the benchmark targets, so the finding is submitted as a lead, not a confirmed match.
